title: Lathyrus palustris

{{Short description|Species of legume}} {{Speciesbox |image = Lathyrus palustris flowers - Kulna.jpg |genus = Lathyrus |species = palustris |authority = [[Carl Linnaeus|L.]] |synonyms = ''Lathyrus myrtifolius''
''Orobus myrtifolius'' }} '''''Lathyrus palustris''''' is a species of [[Lathyrus|wild pea]] known by the common name '''marsh pea'''.{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }} It is native to Europe, Asia, and North America. It is a perennial herb with leaves made up of oval-shaped or oblong leaflets a few centimeters long. It has branched, coiled [[tendril]]s. The plant bears an [[inflorescence]] of two to eight pinkish purple pea flowers each up to two centimeters wide. The fruit is a [[dehiscence (botany)|dehiscent]] legume pod. ==Description== ''Lathyrus linifolius'' is a perennial plant with a sprawling or climbing stem that grows to {{convert|25|to|80|cm|0|abbr=on}} and is shallowly-winged and nearly hairless. The leaves are alternate with short winged stalks and long narrow [[stipule]]s. The leaf blades are pinnate with two to four pairs of narrow lanceolate leaflets, entire margins and a terminal branching tendril. The [[inflorescence]] has a long stem and two to eight purple flowers, each {{convert|12|to|20|mm|1|abbr=on}} long. These have five sepals and five petals and are irregular. The uppermost petal is known as the "standard", the lateral two as the "wings" and the lowest two are joined to form the "keel". There are ten stamens and a single carpel. The fruit is a flat brown pod containing up to twelve seeds. This plant flowers in July and August.{{cite web |url=http://www.luontoportti.com/suomi/en/kukkakasvit/marsh-pea |title=Marsh pea: ''Lathyrus palustris'' |publisher=NatureGate |accessdate=2013-12-31}} ==Distribution and habitat== ''Lathyrus linifolius'' is native to Europe, parts of Asia and North America. Its typical habitat is in rich ground and this plant is found in damp meadows, on river banks, on the margins of ponds, by lakes and near the sea, and occasionally in coastal hedgerows. It often seems to grow among [[Phragmites|reeds]] (''Phragmites australis''). The species [[epithet]] ''palustris'' is Latin for "of the marsh" and indicates its common habitat. Archibald William Smith {{google books|ahNMkgoNJ7IC|A Gardener's Handbook of Plant Names: Their Meanings and Origins|page=258}} Marsh Pea grows from long rhizomes that allows the plant to spread vegetatively. As the common name implies, Marsh Pea, it is found in wet to moist areas where it can receive adequate sun and also allows other plants to climb on. {{cite web|url=https://www.friendsofthewildflowergarden.org/pages/plants/marshpea.html |title=Marsh Pea, Lathyrus palustris L. |publisher=Friends of the Wild Flower Garden |accessdate=2019-10-13}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[http://ucjeps.berkeley.edu/cgi-bin/get_JM_treatment.pl?3691,3922,3944 Jepson Manual Treatment] *[https://plants.usda.gov/java/profile?symbol=LAPA4 USDA Plants Profile] *{{GRIN}} *[http://calphotos.berkeley.edu/cgi/img_query?query_src=photos_index&where-taxon=Lathyrus+palustris Photo gallery] {{Taxonbar|from=Q159365}} [[Category:Lathyrus|palustris]] [[Category:Flora of Asia]] [[Category:Flora of Europe]] [[Category:Flora of Northern America]] [[Category:Plants described in 1753]] [[Category:Botanical taxa named by Carl Linnaeus]] {{fabeae-stub}}
